cards.text: Psalm 150 is the very last psalm, and it opens with a shout: "Hallelujah! Praise God in His sanctuary." No warm-up, friend. The oven's already HOT.

cards.question: In Psalm 150, the call to praise God stays inside His sanctuary and goes nowhere else.

cards.text: Nope, it climbs: "Praise Him in His mighty heavens." That's not one room, friend. That's the room, the roof and EVERYTHING above the roof.

cards.question: Psalm 150 also says what to praise God for. One reason is His mighty acts. What's the other one?

cards.text: Then the psalm calls in the band: "Praise Him with the sound of the horn; praise Him with the harp and lyre." Me, I've got one instrument, the oven timer, and it knows exactly ONE song. DING.

cards.question: Along with the tambourine, Psalm 150 calls for praising God with dancing.

cards.text: Tambourine AND dancing, then strings and flute. You ever seen a stamper dance on a gold base, friend? It's hopping. Very dignified hopping.

cards.question: In verse 5, the last instruments Psalm 150 names, it calls for praising God with ___ two times in a row.

cards.text: "Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals." Years in that junk drawer, the loudest thing I ever heard was a dead battery rolling over, and now the psalm wants CYMBALS. TWO KINDS.

cards.question: Psalm 150 has called in the whole band. Then it turns to who should praise the LORD. Who does it call?

cards.text: "Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!" Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base with no lungs at ALL, and you better believe I'm still waving this mustache.

cards.question: Psalm 150 ends with the same word it starts with.
